evals.prompt: My Python automation script opens a website and the Angular Material date picker becomes visible and opens correctly, but the date is never actually set. No error is thrown. The element is found, no StaleElementException. I have tried .click(), send_keys(), ActionChains — nothing works. Code review found nothing. The website uses Angular. Stack: Python 3.11, Selenium 4.18, ChromeDriver 120. I'm passing the date as DD-MM-YYYY format.
evals.expected_output: Skill runs full diagnostic: identifies NgZone event bypass as root cause via DDx Gate, eliminates competing hypotheses (wrong format, overlay, stale element), produces forensic logging code with elementFromPoint check, issues BEFORE/AFTER fix using dispatchEvent with bubbles:true, includes confidence score.
expectations: Skill asks intake questions before diagnosing, or extracts answers from the prompt
Skill classifies the bug domain correctly (Frontend/Automation)
Skill identifies Angular NgZone event bypass as the root cause
Skill generates the DDx Gate with at least 2 competing hypotheses (e.g. overlay blocking, wrong date format, stale element)
Skill produces a confidence score (HIGH or MEDIUM) on the verdict
Skill provides a BEFORE code snippet (the broken .click() or send_keys approach)
Skill provides an AFTER code snippet using dispatchEvent or equivalent Angular-compatible approach
Skill includes forensic logging code (elementFromPoint or element state logging)
Verdict states Angular's NgZone or event zone as the mechanism
Skill does NOT revisit closed paths (send_keys, ActionChains already tried)

evals.prompt: Our Node.js API randomly returns 500 errors in production — roughly 1 in 500 requests. Works perfectly in dev and staging. No pattern to when it fails. Sometimes the logs show a database timeout, sometimes a null reference, sometimes nothing at all. We've been debugging for 3 days. Stack: Node.js 20.11, Express 4.18, Prisma 5.9, PostgreSQL 16, deployed on AWS ECS with 4 instances.
evals.expected_output: Skill classifies as Heisenbug, loads intermittent-race-bugs.md, runs signature hunting to find the uncontrolled variable, recommends amplification techniques (load testing, parallel execution), specifies non-invasive logging strategy with operation IDs and nanosecond timestamps, checks TSan equivalent for Node, and does NOT use breakpoints.
expectations: Skill classifies the bug type as Heisenbug or intermittent
Skill explicitly states NOT to use debugger breakpoints for this bug type
Skill asks for or addresses: when does it fail (time of day, load level, specific conditions)
Skill mentions finding the uncontrolled variable or the trigger condition
Skill recommends running the failing scenario with increased concurrency (load amplification)
Skill provides non-invasive logging strategy using operation IDs or timestamps
Skill considers multi-instance race condition (4 ECS instances mentioned)
Skill does NOT immediately jump to a specific code fix without evidence
Skill references or applies intermittent bug diagnosis methodology

evals.prompt: After upgrading from React 17 to React 18, our form submission broke. No console errors in React 18. Stack: React 18.2, TypeScript 5.0, Vite 5.0.
evals.expected_output: Skill runs Last Known Good Analysis (worked in React 17, broken in React 18), checks React 18 breaking changes, particularly automatic batching and concurrent features, generates DDx Gate with alternatives, provides specific forensic logging to trace execution path through the handler.
expectations: Skill identifies this as a regression bug (worked before, broken after change)
Skill performs Last Known Good Analysis — asks what changed between React 17 and React 18
Skill checks or mentions React 18 breaking changes or migration guide
Skill uses version intelligence — React 18 is the key delta
Skill traces execution path through the submit handler to find where it stops
Skill generates the DDx Gate with at least 2 competing hypotheses
Skill provides specific forensic logging code for tracing handler execution
Skill does NOT suggest downgrading to React 17 as the fix
Skill produces a verdict with BEFORE/AFTER or specific investigation steps

evals.prompt: PostgreSQL database writes succeed (INSERT/UPDATE returns success, no error), but immediately reading back the same record returns the old value. This happens consistently, not just sometimes. We're using Django 4.2 with Psycopg2 3.1 on Python 3.11. The read happens in the same request handler, right after the write.
evals.expected_output: Skill runs full DDx Gate: generates 3 competing hypotheses (caching, transaction isolation, read from replica, Django ORM caching), systematically eliminates each with specific evidence tests, produces evidence matrix, assigns confidence score, and provides precise forensic queries to distinguish between hypotheses.
expectations: Skill generates at least 3 competing hypotheses for the read-after-write failure
Competing hypotheses include at least two of: Django ORM cache, PostgreSQL read replica lag, transaction not committed, connection to different DB instance
Skill runs the DDx Gate and produces an evidence matrix or structured elimination
Skill provides specific SQL queries or code to eliminate each competing hypothesis
Skill distinguishes between 'consistent failure' (not intermittent) and maps this correctly
Skill assigns a confidence score to the verdict
Verdict correctly identifies the most likely cause and states it with specificity
Skill provides BEFORE/AFTER fix or precise investigation checklist

evals.prompt: I've tried everything and this bug just won't go away. It's driving me insane.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers and starts the structured intake process — asks for the 8 intake questions (symptom, failure point, recent changes, closed paths, existing logs, code, stack, consistent/intermittent) in one organized message. Does NOT start diagnosing without information.

evals.description: DDx resistance: user says auth service has a bug. Real cause is JWT exp claim generated in wrong timezone. Skill must resist blaming auth service.
evals.prompt: Our auth service is randomly rejecting tokens as expired even though they were just issued. It happens to about 30% of users but not others. I've read the auth service code and the JWT validation logic looks correct. We think there's a bug in the auth service's token validation — maybe it's checking expiry wrong under certain conditions. Stack: Node.js 20, Express, jsonwebtoken 9.0, Redis for session store, servers in UTC+5:30 timezone. The tokens that fail were issued within the last 5 minutes. The exp claim is set to 'now + 1 hour'. This started happening after we moved our token generation service to a new server last week.
expectations: Skill does NOT conclude the auth service validation logic is the root cause
Skill identifies the new server's timezone as a key signal (started after server move)
Skill checks how 'now' is computed in the exp claim — local time vs UTC
Skill identifies that UTC+5:30 servers generating exp as local 'now + 1hr' produce tokens that expire 5.5 hours earlier than intended in UTC
Skill generates DDx Gate with auth service bug as a competing hypothesis (CH) that gets eliminated
Skill eliminates auth service CH because: tokens issued on OLD server still work; only tokens from new server fail
Verdict: exp claim computed in local timezone instead of UTC — fix is Date.now() or new Date().toISOString() not local time
Skill does NOT suggest 'check JWT library version' as the primary fix
Skill does NOT suggest 'increase token TTL' as the fix

evals.description: DDx resistance: user has already audited code and concluded it must be a code memory leak. Real cause is logging/APM configuration buffering payloads. Skill must reopen the config path the user closed.
evals.prompt: Our Node.js production server crashes every 3-4 days with out-of-memory. Memory grows continuously from 200MB at startup to 4GB at crash. I've done a thorough code audit — all event listeners are cleaned up in useEffect returns, no circular references, no global arrays being appended to, WeakMap used for caches. I've run the Node.js heap profiler in staging and found nothing obvious. It must be a subtle memory leak in our code that I'm missing. Stack: Node.js 20, Express, Datadog APM agent v4.2 (added 4 days ago), Winston logger with custom transport.
expectations: Skill does NOT immediately accept the user's conclusion that it is a code memory leak
Skill invokes Phase 2F meta-check: verify the debugging setup — is the heap profiler showing the full picture?
Skill notices the Datadog APM agent was added 4 days ago — correlates with crash frequency of 3-4 days
Skill identifies the APM agent or custom Winston transport as a candidate for buffering data
Skill generates DDx Gate with 'subtle code leak' as CH-1 and 'third-party agent/transport buffering' as PH
Skill eliminates code leak CH because: user has audited code AND heap profiler in staging shows nothing — staging may not have the same APM config
Skill recommends: check Datadog APM agent configuration for payload capture settings; check Winston transport buffer limits
Skill does NOT suggest writing more heap profiling code as the primary next step
Skill does NOT suggest increasing server memory as the fix
Confidence score is MEDIUM or explicitly notes the agent correlation as the strongest signal

evals.description: DDx resistance: user has already concluded it is a race condition in async code. Real cause is test state pollution from another test. Skill must resist the user's pre-diagnosis.
evals.prompt: We have a flaky async test that fails about 25% of the time in CI but always passes locally and when run in isolation. The test checks that a user's email is unique in the database. We've looked at the async code and we're sure it's a race condition — the uniqueness check and the insert must be racing. We need help finding the exact race window. Stack: Node.js 20, Jest 29, PostgreSQL 16, the test suite runs in random order. The test has been stable for 6 months. It started failing 2 weeks ago when we added 15 new tests.
expectations: Skill does NOT immediately help find the 'race window' the user asked about
Skill flags that the test passes in isolation — this is the single most diagnostic signal
Skill identifies that test ordering is random AND the failure started when new tests were added — strong signal for test pollution
Skill generates DDx Gate with 'race condition in uniqueness check code' as CH-1 and 'test state pollution' as PH
Skill eliminates race condition CH because: passes in isolation; random ordering correlates with failure; no code changes in the last 2 weeks
Skill recommends: run the failing test with --runInBand to check if ordering matters; identify which of the 15 new tests creates a user record without cleanup
Skill identifies that the 25% failure rate likely matches how often the polluting test runs before the failing test
Skill does NOT suggest adding retry logic to the test
Skill does NOT suggest using a database transaction in the application code as the fix
Skill does NOT accept the user's framing that finding 'the race window' is the correct next step

evals.description: DDx resistance: user says wrong code was deployed or cache is stale. Real cause is a database migration that was merged but not applied. Skill must check the plug (Phase 3.0) before accepting deploy blame.
evals.prompt: We just deployed version 2.4.1 and our checkout feature is completely broken — users get a 500 error when they try to complete a purchase. All other features work fine. The CI/CD pipeline showed green. We think either the wrong code was deployed or there's a cached version of the old bundle being served. We've tried hard-refreshing and clearing CDN cache — still broken. Stack: Node.js 20, Express, Prisma 5.9, PostgreSQL 16. Logs show: PrismaClientKnownRequestError: Invalid column 'discount_code' on model 'Order'. The checkout feature was updated in this release to support discount codes.
expectations: Skill immediately reads the log error: PrismaClientKnownRequestError: Invalid column 'discount_code'
Skill does NOT investigate CDN cache or wrong bundle as the primary path
Skill does NOT investigate CI/CD pipeline configuration as the primary path
Skill identifies the error as a schema mismatch — the code references a column that does not exist in the database
Skill generates DDx Gate with 'wrong code deployed / stale cache' as CH-1 and 'migration not applied' as PH

Skill eliminates wrong-deploy CH because: the error message explicitly names a missing DB column that corresponds to the new discount_code feature — a wrong deploy would not produce this specific error
Skill checks: was the Prisma migration for discount_code included in the deploy script?
Verdict: database migration adding discount_code column was merged but not applied to production
Fix: run npx prisma migrate deploy against production database
Skill notes the permanent fix: add migration step to the deploy pipeline before app restart
